tasks.short: Plan and teach mobile robot paths

steps.what: Inspect the actual mobile robot operating area, obstacles, access constraints and intended destinations
inputs: actual robot mission and working area
actual people, equipment and operating restrictions
outputs: engineer's observed route constraints and mission requirements

steps.what: Plan mobile robot paths, choosing actual route, waypoints, clearances, speeds and exception behavior
inputs: engineer's observed route constraints and mission requirements
actual robot capabilities and operating limits
outputs: engineer-selected actual path plan and constraints

steps.what: Enter and check the exact final path plan, waypoint identities, speed limits and intended offline route record in robot path-planning software (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: engineer-selected actual path plan and constraints
actual robot/route identity and engineer-entered waypoint coordinates
outputs: exact checked final path plan and offline record destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked path plan in the intended offline route record
inputs: exact checked final path plan and offline record destination
outputs: saved exact planned route revision

steps.what: Check actual robot identity, saved exact route revision, teaching mode, clear area and readiness immediately before physical path teaching
inputs: saved exact planned route revision
actual robot, area condition and authorised teaching limits
outputs: checked final route/robot match and current physical teaching readiness

steps.what: Teach path plans to robots through supervised physical teaching and observation of the exact checked planned route within authorised limits
inputs: checked final route/robot match and current physical teaching readiness
actual live robot motion and area condition
outputs: actual taught path and observed teaching outcome or stopped attempt

tasks.design: Configure native waypoint/property entry presets in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the robot path-planning/teaching system. The engineer inspects the real area, chooses and checks the actual route, saves that exact plan and checks physical readiness before supervised teaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated fixed route/robot properties add path-entry effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native planning presets can reuse fixed identifiers and entry settings.
tasks.still_hard: Real obstacles, people and localization behavior require physical supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the route and stop teaching when real conditions differ.

ambition.what: No autonomous route deployment or unsupervised teaching.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; robot/area owners validate teaching permissions and presets

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native route-entry presets can reduce repeated fixed fields while path selection and physical robot teaching remain engineering work.

assumptions: Unmeasured path-planning/teaching episode. Gross 19 x .10 = 1.9; upkeep .75; net 1.15 hours per 100.
Engineer observes the area in s1, chooses path in s2 and enters actual waypoints in s3. No free map, obstacle feed or automatically valid route is assumed.
Same-system offline save is 1 fully retained point with no saving; native robot planning/runtime already used today earn no saving.

s3 checks exact final offline plan/destination before s4. s5 then checks actual robot, saved final route and current conditions before the distinct physical teach action s6. Any route/robot/condition change voids readiness and requires recheck.
Teaching includes live observation and stopping, not an unattended script. A changed path returns through authoring/checking and each actual write; no additional report or follow-up send is promised.
unknowns: Actual repeated route-entry fields and existing presets
research_questions: Which fixed fields are re-entered separately from genuine route decisions and physical teaching?

already_counted.description: Area inspection, route decisions, final entry/check and physical readiness/teaching

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed path plan and offline record destination checked in s3; edits require recheck
Exact saved final route, robot, teaching mode and current area readiness checked in s5; any change requires renewed check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 entry-preset scenario below 1.15% modeled net; physical teaching retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Study the actual green-product manufacturing operation, such as solar-panel handling, its production-time objectives, waste and cost constraints
inputs: actual manufacturer process and workpieces
actual stated production-time, waste and cost objectives with available evidence
outputs: engineer-observed manufacturing requirements and evidence gaps

steps.what: Design robotics applications for manufacturers of green products to address actual production-time, waste or cost objectives, choosing handling, sensing and robot integration
inputs: engineer-observed manufacturing requirements and evidence gaps
actual product fragility, equipment interfaces and operating constraints
outputs: engineer-selected robotic application design and supported trade-offs

steps.what: Author actual robotic cell layout, handling interfaces and application model in robotic cell engineering software (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: engineer-selected robotic application design and supported trade-offs
engineer-entered real equipment/workpiece dimensions and component properties
outputs: complete robotic application model and design draft

steps.what: Check the completed green-product robotic application against physical requirements, assumptions and actual production/waste/cost evidence
inputs: complete robotic application model and design draft
actual requirements, evidence gaps and internal revision destination
outputs: exact checked application design, limitations and intended internal destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked robotic application design as its intended internal revision
inputs: exact checked application design, limitations and intended internal destination
outputs: saved internal green-product robotic application design

tasks.design: For a solar-panel handling application, configure native equipment/component layout reuse in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the robotic cell engineering system. The engineer studies the actual manufacturing process, chooses the application design and checks the completed model and claims before saving the exact internal revision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated cell equipment and component drafting adds model-entry effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native engineering libraries can reuse known layout components.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile products, process variation and production economics require actual manufacturing evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Choose useful automation and reject unsupported production or waste claims.

ambition.what: No invented baseline or promised manufacturer performance gain.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; manufacturing/design owners validate geometry access and library use

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native robotic cell component reuse can reduce drafting while manufacturing-application design and performance claims require real process evidence.

assumptions: Unmeasured solar-panel handling design episode, one stated green-product example. Gross 24 x .15 = 3.6; upkeep 1; net 2.6 hours per 100.
Engineer observes actual process and enters dimensions/properties in s1-s3. No free digital factory, production baseline or measured waste reduction is assumed.

Task wording's production-time objective is treated as the manufacturer's actual stated objective, without inventing a throughput improvement. Existing CAD/simulation runtime already happens today and earns no saving.

Same-system save 1 stays fully retained with no saving. Final full-design check s4 gates exact internal revision and destination; edits invalidate it. No machine deployment or external customer send is promised.
unknowns: Existing component reuse and actual repeated layout work
research_questions: Which actual cell components are redrawn, and what evidence supports the manufacturer's intended outcome?

already_counted.description: Actual manufacturing study, application design and complete-model verification

incremental.description: Maintain and check reusable cell geometry/component properties

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed robotic application design, limits and destination checked in s4; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 repeated-layout scenario below 2.6% modeled net; no unmeasured production benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review the actual assay method, laboratory robot capability, labware, samples and acceptance requirements
inputs: actual assay method from its laboratory method owner
actual robot, labware and assay acceptance requirements
outputs: engineer-reviewed assay and equipment constraints

steps.what: Translate the actual assay into robotic liquid-handling sequence, volumes, timing, labware positions and error handling
inputs: engineer-reviewed assay and equipment constraints
actual laboratory method-owner clarification of ambiguities
outputs: engineer-authored actual assay automation sequence and parameters

steps.what: Author the laboratory robotic assay protocol in laboratory robot programming software (OPS_SYSTEM), using actual parameters and labware definitions
inputs: engineer-authored actual assay automation sequence and parameters
actual robot/labware definitions and validated reusable primitives
outputs: complete candidate robotic assay protocol

steps.what: Check the final complete assay protocol offline, including volumes, timing, deck positions, error paths, robot identity and intended protocol destination
inputs: complete candidate robotic assay protocol
actual assay method and authored automation sequence
outputs: exact final checked robotic assay protocol and intended robot protocol destination

steps.what: Commit the exact checked assay protocol to the intended robot protocol record for controlled validation
inputs: exact final checked robotic assay protocol and intended robot protocol destination
outputs: actual committed exact assay validation protocol

steps.what: Check exact committed protocol, actual robot deck, labware, validation materials and current run readiness within authorised lab conditions
inputs: actual committed exact assay validation protocol
actual labware/deck state, validation materials and authorised conditions
outputs: checked exact validation protocol/setup and current run readiness

steps.what: Run and observe the exact checked robotic assay validation, measure actual outcomes and intervene on failures
inputs: checked exact validation protocol/setup and current run readiness
actual assay validation measurements and robot behavior
outputs: actual assay automation validation results and observed exceptions

steps.what: Evaluate actual validation results and enter/check the assay automation record, limitations and exact protocol/run identities
inputs: actual assay automation validation results and observed exceptions
actual assay acceptance criteria and protocol/run identifiers
outputs: exact checked validation record and intended internal run destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked robotic assay validation record in its intended internal run record
inputs: exact checked validation record and intended internal run destination
outputs: saved actual assay automation validation record

tasks.design: Configure reusable validated protocol primitives and labware definitions in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the laboratory robot programming/validation system. The engineer translates the actual assay, authors and checks the final protocol, commits it and checks physical readiness before validation, then records and checks the actual outcome before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated labware and protocol primitive setup adds assay implementation effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native laboratory robot method libraries can reduce repeated protocol authoring.
tasks.still_hard: Assay validity, liquid behavior, deck state and failure handling need real laboratory validation.
tasks.human_edge: Translate the biological/chemical method correctly and detect invalid automation outcomes.

ambition.what: No automatic method validation or production assay release.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3; method and lab owners validate primitives, permissions and validation conditions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native laboratory robot method libraries can reduce repeated protocol authoring, while assay translation and physical validation remain necessary.

assumptions: Unmeasured assay-automation development episode. Gross 25 x .20 = 5; upkeep 1.5; net 3.5 hours per 100.

Laboratory method owner provides the actual assay; engineer captures interpretation, sequence and parameters in s1-s3. Ambiguity stops implementation for method-owner clarification, not inferred volumes or timing.
Existing robot execution already happens today and earns no saving. Only repeated programming setup changes; all validation and record work remains counted.

Protocol commit and final record save each carry 1 fully retained point, approximately zero today and no saving. Offline exact-protocol check s4 gates s5, current physical readiness s6 gates the distinct run action s7, and completed actual record check s8 gates s9.

Changes to any protocol/setup/conditions void the relevant gate; reruns follow renewed checking. This records development validation and does not claim permission for production assays or formal method release.
unknowns: Existing protocol reuse and actual validation burden
research_questions: Which programming primitives recur without changing assay validity, and what actual validation evidence is required?

already_counted.description: Method translation, remaining protocol authoring, offline/physical checks, validation and final record

incremental.description: Maintain and revalidate reusable protocol primitives and labware definitions

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed protocol and intended robot protocol destination checked in s4; edits require recheck
Exact committed protocol, physical setup and current validation readiness checked in s6; any change requires renewed check
Exact completed actual validation record and internal run destination checked in s8; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 native protocol reuse scenario below 3.5% modeled net; no robot-runtime or free assay validation benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

skills_to_grow: Keep exact route/protocol versions aligned with physical readiness
Translate actual assay methods without inferred parameters
Validate reusable engineering primitives against application-specific conditions
role.ambitious_version: Reduce repeated route, cell-model and assay protocol entry with validated native libraries while retaining physical observation, application design, method interpretation and every robot action gate.
